subtopics.title: Scarcity, Choice and the Economic Problem

questions.question: Scarcity is best described as:
options: The permanent condition of limited resources facing unlimited wants — present in every economy, rich or poor
A temporary shortage caused by a bad season
An empty shelf at one shop
A problem only developing countries face

questions.question: The learner takes a Saturday car-wash shift and gives up sleep, series and a soccer trial that mattered most. The opportunity cost of the shift is:
options: Sleep, series and the trial added together
The soccer trial only — the single next best alternative sacrificed
The wage earned at the car wash
Nothing, since the shift paid money

questions.question: The three fundamental questions every society answers are:
options: Where, when and why to produce
Save, spend or invest
WHAT to produce, HOW to produce it, and FOR WHOM
Import, export or manufacture

questions.question: On the production possibility curve, a country with unemployment above thirty percent is producing:
options: On the curve, efficiently
Beyond the curve
At the origin
INSIDE the curve — resources idle, output below the attainable maximum

subtopics.title: The Circular Flow and the National Numbers

questions.question: The three leakages from the circular flow are:
options: Saving, taxation and spending on imports
Investment, government spending and exports
Wages, rent and profit
GDP, GNI and per capita income

questions.question: The flow of income EXPANDS when:
options: Leakages exceed injections
Injections — investment, government spending and export revenue — exceed leakages
Households stop selling factors of production
Saving rises while investment falls

questions.question: A German-owned plant producing in Gqeberha counts in South African GDP because:
options: Its profits are paid in rand
It employs South African managers
GDP obeys the WHERE rule — production within the borders counts, whoever owns the factors
GDP obeys the WHO rule — ownership decides

questions.question: The blind spots of GDP include:
options: Exports, imports and taxes
Wages, interest and rent
Final goods and market prices
Unpaid household work, undercounted informal activity, invisible distribution, and environmental damage booked as nothing

questions.question: Equilibrium is the price at which:
options: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied — buyers' and sellers' plans agree, with no surplus and no shortage
Sellers earn maximum profit
Government fixes the market
Demand is at its highest point

questions.question: The only thing that causes a MOVEMENT along a product's demand curve is:
options: A change in consumer income
A change in the product's OWN price
A change in the price of a substitute
A change in the number of buyers

questions.question: Avian flu strikes poultry farms. The correct four-step reading for the egg market is:
options: Demand shifts right; surplus; price falls; larger quantity
Demand shifts left; shortage; price rises; larger quantity
Supply shifts LEFT; shortage at the old price; price rises; new equilibrium at higher price and smaller quantity
Supply shifts right; surplus; price falls; smaller quantity

questions.question: In a price-quantity table, at any price ABOVE the equilibrium row you find:
options: Excess demand, calculated as demand minus supply
Equilibrium at every row
A shortage that bids prices up
EXCESS SUPPLY, calculated as quantity supplied minus quantity demanded

subtopics.title: Markets, Value and the Business Cycle

questions.question: Water is essential yet cheap where abundant, while near-useless diamonds command fortunes, because VALUE requires:
options: BOTH utility and scarcity together
Utility alone
Government price-setting
High production costs

questions.question: A handful of large firms watching each other's every move — like banking or mobile networks — is classified as:
options: Perfect competition
OLIGOPOLY
Monopoly
Monopolistic competition

questions.question: The four phases of the business cycle in fixed order are:
options: Prosperity, recovery, depression, recession
Depression, recession, prosperity, recovery
Recovery, prosperity, recession, depression
Recession, recovery, depression, prosperity

questions.question: Building plans approved, current retail sales, and unemployment are respectively:
options: Lagging, leading, coincident indicators
Coincident, lagging, leading indicators
All coincident indicators
LEADING, COINCIDENT and LAGGING indicators

questions.question: The R350 wallet against the R580 fridge list teaches that:
options: The gap between means and wants is permanent — scarcity, not a bad month
The family budgeted badly
Prices are too high this month only
Saving more would end scarcity

questions.question: The family buys soccer boots for R350; the best alternative was the month's data and taxi fare. The true cost of the boots is:
options: R350 on the till slip
The data and taxi fare — the top alternative walked away from
Everything else on the fridge list combined
Nothing, because boots were needed

questions.question: In the sewing room picture of the economy, two machines standing idle means production is:
options: On the curve
Beyond the curve
INSIDE the curve — the room producing less than it could, the picture of unemployment
Impossible to place on the curve

subtopics.title: The Circle of Money on One Street

questions.question: On the Saturday main road, the three LEAKS from the street's circle of money are:
options: Money saved in the bank, money taxed away, and money spent on imported goods
Wages, lunches and haircuts
The fryer, the clinic and the rooibos sales
Fish, paint and braids

questions.question: The fish shop buying a second fryer, the clinic being repainted with government money, and rooibos sold abroad are examples of:
options: The three leakages
The three INJECTIONS — investment, government spending and export earnings
Household consumption only
Taxes flowing to the state

questions.question: Counting the parcel of fish and chips but NOT also the potatoes inside it applies the rule that GDP counts:
options: Imported goods at the border
Every transaction twice for accuracy
Only FINAL goods — counting intermediate inputs would double-count
Only goods, never services

questions.question: The foreign-owned franchise on the corner counts in South Africa's GDP, but its profits sent home are handled by:
options: Adding them to GDP a second time
Ignoring them in all accounts
Counting them as a government injection
GNI — which follows income to the owners' nationality, subtracting what foreign owners remit home

subtopics.title: The Argument That Sets the Price, and the Economy That Breathes

questions.question: Vetkoek at fifteen rand leave a full tray at ten o'clock; at three rand the tray empties before assembly. This shows:
options: Prices above equilibrium leave surpluses and prices below leave shortages — the market argues its way to the crossing point
Learners dislike vetkoek at any price
The seller should always choose the lowest price
Equilibrium requires a committee to set it

questions.question: The price of cooking oil doubles, raising the stand's costs. For the vetkoek market this causes:
options: A movement along the supply curve only
A SHIFT of the whole supply curve — something other than the product's own price changed first
A movement along the demand curve only
No change at all

questions.question: The reflex sentence for movement versus shift is:
options: Any change anywhere shifts every curve
Curves shift only when government intervenes
The product's OWN price moves you along the curve; everything else moves the curve itself
Demand curves shift but supply curves never do

questions.question: In the breathing economy, headlights, speedometer and rearview mirror stand for:
options: The four phases of the cycle
Internal and external causes of the cycle
Perfect, imperfect and monopoly markets
Leading indicators seeing ahead, coincident indicators reading the present, and lagging indicators confirming the past
